<p class="g-kicker">The real science · cleaner wrasse</p>
<h1>A service economy on a coral reef.</h1>
<p class="g-lede">The cleaner-wrasse mutualism is one of the best-studied cooperation systems
in nature: a marketplace with clients, cheating, punishment, and reputation.
Here's the science behind each mechanic.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section class="g-main">
<div class="g-inner">
<div class="g-prose">

<h2>Two thousand clients a day</h2>
<p>The bluestreak cleaner wrasse (<em>Labroides dimidiatus</em>) holds a small territory, a
"cleaning station," where other fish come to have their ectoparasites picked off. A single
cleaner inspects on the order of <strong>2,300 clients per day</strong> and eats over a
thousand parasites doing it<sup><a href="#ref-1">1</a></sup>. Clients queue, pose with fins
spread, and hold still for a stranger's mouth. Both sides profit, as long as both sides
behave.</p>

<h2>The temptation</h2>
<p>Here's the catch that makes it a cooperation problem: given the choice, cleaners
<strong>prefer client mucus over parasites</strong><sup><a href="#ref-2">2</a></sup>. Every
honest inspection is a small act of self-restraint. Cheating (biting mucus) makes the client
visibly jolt, which is what makes the system measurable in the field.</p>

<h2>Partner control</h2>
<p>What keeps cleaners honest is that clients have options. <strong>Resident</strong> clients
with small home ranges are stuck with their local cleaner, and they respond to cheats by
punishing (chasing the cleaner around the coral, which costs it foraging time).
<strong>Visitors</strong> with large ranges simply leave and take their custom to a rival
station<sup><a href="#ref-3">3</a></sup>. Cleaners essentially never cheat
<strong>predatory clients</strong>, where the "punishment" would be getting eaten.</p>

<h2>Reputation</h2>
<p>Bystander clients observe ongoing interactions and use what they see. In experiments,
clients preferentially approached cleaners they had watched cooperating and avoided ones they
had seen cheat<sup><a href="#ref-4">4</a></sup>. A cleaner's honesty toward the client in
front of it is simultaneously an advertisement to everyone in line, which is why, in the game,
cheating with a bystander present costs future customers.</p>

<h2>The massage</h2>
<p>A cleaner can also hover above a client and drum its pelvic fins along the client's back, a
"massage" that provides no food. Experiments show cleaners use it strategically to entice new
partners, calm predators, and <strong>reconcile with clients they've just cheated</strong>
<sup><a href="#ref-5">5</a></sup>. The touch itself is a genuine service because it measurably
lowers client stress hormones<sup><a href="#ref-6">6</a></sup>.</p>
